not_run.trace_norm_leakage_S_infinity_and_2: Ill-posed as drafted. A trace norm is nonnegative, so leakage cannot be assigned a negative sign. A future test must bound the nonnegative norm and, separately, a signed quadratic remainder, and only then discuss decay.

corrections_applied_on_top_of_the_bundle: Status is not 'nothing claims progress.' Structural refinements and consistency tests; no new positivity theorem.
Counterterm is finite: M_N = -K(0) + 2 sum_{n<=N} a_n, N >= exp(A), F zero outside the window. The uncutoff sum diverges. Tails past the window cancel.
Rayleigh form without the pole is for F in E0. Off E0 the pole term remains.
E0 on the log line is dense in L2 and not closed. Tate b(f) is a different space, linked by smearing.
Finite-field samples are not continuous Mellin moments. The figure uses Frobenius iterates n=0,1,2.
There is no universal identity 'every mechanism is a square plus an indefinite boundary.'

Connes 1999: global trace formula <=> RH for all Groessencharakter L-functions (over Q: zeta and all Dirichlet). In char p, Delta subtracts Q'_{Lambda,0} from S_Lambda. Subtracting a positive operator does not by itself make the difference positive.
II_{1,1} is an analogy. No arithmetic lattice is constructed.
Kaehler anti-self-dual geometry and the Hodge index on C x C (used in Weil RH for curves) are different theorems.

Abstract GNS factorization assuming RH can inherit formal compatibilities and is circular as a proof. The missing piece is independent positivity of H+ identified with W. Not every further demand follows automatically.
On the test core, [Q0, D] = i. They do not commute. Fixed-window self-adjointness needs boundary conditions. Real F is a self-adjoint convolution only if F sharp equals F.
Hessian off the origin is W plus a nonnegative term from a quartic potential with lambda >= 0. The Hessian stays quadratic in the variation.
Free-basis K=8: exactly one negative Galerkin eigenvalue of W-P, numerical, not the exact-E0 spring basis.
h=-1 Virasoro norm is algebra, not a unitarity proof.
